input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: research programme hanger-codesign (pick_track draw): milestone 3a, a triangle FEM top-tier candidate against the exact cantilever elastica and the Cusick acceptance test
errors: First fem.py had a sign error in the hinge (dihedral) gradient; my first finite-difference check used a random direction dominated by the membrane and missed it. Found when a pilot cantilever did not move; fixed before any prediction was evaluated, and test_m3 now checks bending alone.
Hinge constant first set to the textbook B theta^2 |e|^2/(A1+A2); a cylinder check gave 1.9x the continuum energy on an equilateral lattice (cross-edge folds); halved before any run.
Newton's first Hessian used forward differences, which gave spurious negative eigenvalues (~1 N/m) at the flat state; switched to central differences.
Started the experiment chain with a shell '&' inside a foreground Bash call rather than run_in_background; it survived, but output was invisible until each part finished.
9 of 32 Cusick cases hit the 400-step Newton cap (8 on fabric A); reported as unconverged with their residuals rather than as equilibria.
integrity_issues: Predictions F1 to F6 were committed before any run; the solver was changed after a pilot in which one 16-element cantilever result and one 8-element smoke-test result were seen. Predictions were not changed; this is disclosed in run.py's docstring, LOG.md and the README. F7 was added with the solver change, before its run.

doc_friction.issue: Says research-ci runs a project's tests implicitly ('test counts...'); research-ci.yml only builds the homepage and runs programme_check, so project tests (here needing scipy) are verified only locally. Worth one sentence.

--for-changes on a research PR that adds one blog post runs the whole portfolio-pages node suite (over 120 s, handed off) and venture validators; a post-only fast path (check_post_frontmatter first) would have caught the description-length failure in 0.2 s.

deviations.why: Proposal milestone 3 says build and wrap ARCSim or C-IPC; both are C++ builds with native deps, so this step wrote ARCSim's element model in numpy to test whether the element alone passes the acceptance test before investing in a build.
deviations.did: numpy CST + discrete-shell tier with a damped Newton solver
deviations.result: Element fails the Cusick acceptance test; this narrows the top-tier choice to nonconforming/remeshing elements or the real solvers.

deviations.why: Pre-registered solver (chunked L-BFGS) stops 9% short on the cantilever.
deviations.did: Changed to Newton before any prediction was evaluated, disclosed.
deviations.result: Cantilever converged to |g| ~1e-6 node weight; Cusick converged on 23 of 32 cases.

notes: Local checks: tests/ 37 passed (python3.13, numpy+scipy); research/_homepage/build.py ok; research_live_links ok; check_md_links ok; programme_check ok; check_post_frontmatter ok after shortening description/seo_title; run_workflow_locally --for-changes: research-ci and readme-live-links passed, portfolio-pages front-matter failure fixed (the node suite's 168 failures were that same description length), node suite rerun in background. Cusick part 95 min on 4 cores.
